answer: Each agent must register a hardware fingerprint drawn from its chip's physically-unclonable function: tiny manufacturing variations that act like a silicon mirror no two devices share. When the network issues a random challenge, a genuine device returns its unique PUF response; a thousand sybils spun up on one machine all reflect the same fingerprint and collapse into a single admitted identity. Honest agents scatter across a meadow of distinct chips like juniper seeded on open ground, while clones cluster onto detectable shared hardware and get pruned.
